slides.title: Mahagauri, radiant and calm
slides.sub: The eighth form of Durga, worshipped on Ashtami

slides.title: Purity and forgiveness
slides.body: After long austerities the Goddess regains a radiant, fair complexion. Dressed in white, calm and gentle, Mahagauri stands for purity and forgiveness.

slides.title: White, on a bull
slides.body: She rides a bull and holds a trident and a damaru, the small drum. Ashtami is one of the most important days everywhere: kanya pujan in many north Indian homes, anjali and Sandhi Puja in Bengal.

slides.text:
श्वेते वृषे समारूढा श्वेताम्बरधरा शुचिः ।
महागौरी शुभं दद्यान्महादेवप्रमोददा ॥
slides.translit: Shvete vrishe samarudha shvetambaradhara shuchih, mahagauri shubham dadyan mahadevapramodada
slides.meaning: May Mahagauri, pure, robed in white and riding a white bull, the joy of Mahadeva, grant what is good.

slides.title: Day 8 at a glance
items: Short mantra: Om Devi Mahagauryai Namah

slides.title: Sandhi Puja: 48 minutes, 108 lamps
slides.sub: Where Ashtami ends and Navami begins

slides.title: 24 + 24 minutes
slides.body: Sandhi means junction. Sandhi Puja takes the last 24 minutes of Ashtami and the first 24 of Navami: 48 minutes in all, counted by the lunar day (tithi), not the calendar day.

slides.title: When is it this year?
slides.body: Ashtami is Mon 19 Oct, Navami Tue 20 Oct. The junction may fall in the afternoon, late at night or before dawn, on either date. Ask your puja committee or check a reliable local panjika.

slides.title: Durga as Chamunda
slides.body: In the Devi Mahatmya, the fierce Chamunda slays the demon generals Chanda and Munda. Bengali tradition places that battle at this junction, so the goddess is worshipped as Chamunda.

slides.title: 108 lotuses, 108 lamps
items: A symbolic ash gourd, sugarcane or banana

slides.title: Rama's 108th lotus
slides.body: In Krittibas's Bengali Ramayana, Rama gathers 108 blue lotuses for Durga. She hides one to test him, and he resolves to offer his own eye. She stops him and grants him victory.

slides.line: At the junction: dhak, conch and ulu rise together

slides.title: Ask the time. Arrive early.
slides.ask: Send it to the family group

caption.en:
Sandhi Puja 2026 in Kolkata: the 48 minutes at the heart of Durga Puja 🪔

It is the junction where Ashtami ends and Navami begins: the last 24 minutes of one lunar day and the first 24 of the next. The goddess is worshipped as Chamunda, with 108 lotuses and 108 lamps. For many Bengalis it is the most powerful moment of the puja.

This year Maha Ashtami is Monday 19 October and Maha Navami Tuesday 20 October. The junction can fall in the afternoon, late at night or before dawn, so the clock time comes from the panjika your priest follows. Almanacs can differ slightly, and a time from another year or city won't help.

The pandal fills well before the junction, so get there early.

slides.title: Kumari Puja: the goddess in a young girl
slides.sub: Best known at Belur Math, on Ashtami morning

slides.title: Why worship a girl?
slides.body: Shakta tradition teaches that the goddess is present in every woman, and can be worshipped in a girl as purely as in an image. It asks devotees to see the divine in every woman, and honour girls and women.

slides.title: The ritual, step by step
items: She is bathed and dressed in a red sari
Her feet are washed and painted with alta
She is seated near the deity
Worshipped with the same mantras as Durga
Flowers, bel leaves, lamps, incense, food
Devotees, monks and priests bow before her

slides.title: Vivekananda, 1901
slides.body: Swami Vivekananda is widely credited with holding the first Durga Puja at Belur Math in 1901 and worshipping young girls as the goddess there. The Ramakrishna Math has continued it since.

slides.title: Customs vary
slides.body: Generally the girl is under the age of puberty. Many pujas choose a girl from a Brahmin family; some accept girls of any caste or background. Some texts name the goddess differently for each age.

slides.title: Kumari Puja and kanya pujan
slides.body: Kanya pujan, common in North India at Navratri, honours several girls at home with food and gifts. Bengali Kumari Puja is a full ritual worship of one girl, usually in a temple or pandal.

slides.title: Going to Belur Math?
slides.body: It is crowded on Ashtami morning: go early and follow the volunteers. Ask before photographing the Kumari. Check the Math's own announcements for this year's arrangements.

caption.en:
Kumari Puja 2026 at Belur Math near Kolkata: why a young girl is worshipped as Durga 🌺

Most Bengali pujas that hold it, Belur Math included, do so on Maha Ashtami: Monday 19 October this year. Some traditions hold it on Navami or another day, so check with the puja or temple.

The girl is bathed, dressed in a red sari, her feet painted with alta, and worshipped with the same mantras and offerings as the goddess. Swami Vivekananda is widely credited with holding it at Belur Math in 1901.

The idea behind it: the goddess is present in every woman, and can be worshipped in a girl as purely as in an image.

slides.title: Kanya pujan at home, step by step
slides.sub: Honouring young girls as the Goddess

slides.title: What you need
items: A thali, water and a clean towel
Roli and uncooked rice for tilak
Flowers and a lamp for aarti
Puri, kala chana and suji halwa

slides.title: Invite, then cook
slides.body: Follow your family's day, Ashtami or Navami, and invite the girls and their parents a day or two ahead. After bathing, cook puri, kala chana and halwa, and offer a portion to the Goddess first.

slides.title: Welcome, wash their feet
slides.body: Seat the children on clean mats and ask parents about allergies. Gently pour water over each child's feet into a plate and dry them. This act of humility is the heart of the ritual.

slides.title: Tilak, thread, aarti
slides.body: Apply roli and a few grains of rice on each forehead and tie a red thread on the wrist. Offer flowers, do a short aarti and fold your hands, seeing them as the Goddess.

slides.title: Feed them, then gifts
slides.body: Serve puri, chana and halwa and let them eat at their own pace. Give each a small gift, bow and ask for their blessings. Many families then break their Navratri fast.

slides.title: Kumari Puja
slides.body: Bengal's own form is Kumari Puja on Maha Ashtami: a priest worships one young girl as the Goddess, often at Belur Math. Kanya pujan is a home ritual for several children with a meal.

slides.title: Save this for Ashtami or Navami
slides.bn: অষ্টমী বা নবমীর জন্য রেখে দিন

caption.en:
Kanya pujan at home this Navratri and Durga Puja: the steps, the meal and the gifts 🌸

Families invite girls, commonly aged about 2 to 10, and often one boy as langur or Bhairav. You wash their feet, apply tilak and tie a red thread. Then you feed them puri, kala chana and halwa, give small gifts and ask for their blessings.

How many girls? Nine, for the nine forms of Durga, is the ideal many aim for, but any number invited with sincerity is accepted. Bengal's own form is Kumari Puja on Maha Ashtami, often at Belur Math.
